title: 7/26/2026 | John B. Bradley - Lazy S Ranch | LTRS | Pro se Intervenor writing to support Texas State Representatives in urging the Public Utility Commission to delay its final decision on the massive 765-kV transmission line segments.

=== Letter of Support to PUC State Reps.pdf ===
John B. Bradley
Lazy S Ranch
16767 Crows Ranch Road
Salado, TX 76571


July 26th, 2026


The Honorable Thomas Gleeson, Chair
Commissioners of the Public Utility Commission of Texas
1701 N. Congress Avenue
Austin, TX 78701

SUBJECT: Support for Legislative Request to Delay 765-kV Transmission Line Decision

Dear Chairman Gleeson and Commissioners,

I am writing to formally express my strong support for the recent letter submitted by our
State Representatives, which requests a necessary delay in the final decision regarding the
proposed 765-kV transmission line segments until after the 90th Legislative Session.

As an active-duty senior Army leader, my profession requires evaluating complex, high-
stakes environments where decisions carry generational consequences. In military
operations, when faced with rapidly changing variables, a lack of informed clarity, and
incomplete intelligence, the most prudent course of action is to exercise tactical patience.

Currently, the landscape of Texas power generation is shifting drastically—most notably
with the massive surge of natural gas generation entering the interconnection queue and
the evolving energy demands of new technology sectors. Moving forward with a permanent,
multi-billion-dollar cross-state transmission project based on outdated assumptions fails
to establish the shared understanding required for an infrastructure commitment of this
magnitude.

Committing to this 765-kV buildout right now introduces an unacceptable level of strategic
and economic risk. By rushing this timeline, we are bypassing the opportunity to fully
assess viable alternatives, specifically the expansion of localized, reliable power
generation that could secure our grid without relying on vulnerable, cross-state
transmission corridors that permanently impact thousands of Texas landowners.

I urge the Commission to heed the Representatives' call. Pausing this decision to allow
ERCOT and the Legislature to conduct a modernized, comprehensive reappraisal is not a
 delay of progress; it is a necessary tactical pause to ensure we execute the most effective,
resilient plan for the future of Texas.

Thank you for your time, your service to the State of Texas, and your careful consideration of
this matter.

Sincerely,



John B. Bradley
Pro se Intervenor
Lazy S Ranch
